blogTitle: What's the Average Cost to Hire an Interior Decorator?
videoTitle: What's the Average Cost to Hire an Interior Decorator?
script:
What's the Average Cost to Hire an Interior Decorator?

[warmly] You know that feeling when you walk into a room and everything just… FITS — the colours, the art, the whole vibe?

So — today we're covering EVERYTHING about interior decorator costs in the UK, from hourly rates right through to full home makeovers…

Okay — first up, the pricing MODELS, because this is where a lot of people get caught off guard…

The most common is the HOURLY rate — anywhere from £30 to £150 an hour depending on experience and where you live, you know?

Then there's a FIXED fee — some decorators charge a set amount for a specific project, like redesigning one room, which honestly makes budgeting so much easier…

And for bigger projects, decorators often charge a PERCENTAGE of the total budget — usually ten to twenty percent — which covers design, sourcing, the whole lot…

[curious] So what does it actually COST in the UK? A single room — think living room or bedroom — typically runs between £1,000 and £2,500…

Doing a few rooms or an open-plan space? That can range from around £5,000 up to £15,000 — it really depends on materials and how much custom work is involved…

And a FULL home makeover? That starts at £20,000 and up — especially once bespoke furniture or imported pieces come into the picture…

Now — what actually DRIVES the cost up or down? Let's talk about the main factors…

First — room SIZE and scope… a simple refresh costs a lot less than a redesign with bespoke cabinetry and upholstery, trust me…

MATERIALS matter too — silk curtains and rare wood push the budget up, but there are brilliant calm, stylish alternatives that don't break the bank…

Project TIMELINE is a big one — rush jobs can push costs up with expedited shipping or overtime, so plan ahead if you can…

LOCATION plays a role too — city-centre decorators often charge more than those in rural areas, partly due to travel and supplier costs…

And then there's LEVEL of involvement — some clients want to be hands-on and source their own pieces, others hand everything over completely… both are totally valid…

[gently] So how do you actually BUDGET for all this without getting overwhelmed? Start by knowing your total figure — and build from there…

A little tip I love: break it down by room and pricing model — get a few quotes, compare them against the scope, and you'll immediately feel more in CONTROL…

[excited] And here's something people don't always realise — a good interior decorator can actually SAVE you money in the long run…

They avoid costly MISTAKES — wrong paint colours, furniture that doesn't fit, pieces that clash — things that add up fast when you're doing it alone…

Now — smart wall art choices are honestly one of the BEST ways to reduce your decorator costs without sacrificing style…

A set of PRINTS like this can anchor a whole room without the cost of bespoke artwork — and the impact is immediate…

These Asian-inspired prints are calm, considered… the kind of wall art that makes a room feel FINISHED without overpowering it…

And honestly — swapping out wall art is one of the QUICKEST ways to refresh a room without touching the decorator's budget at all…

[warmly] Urban, graphic, a little bold… this set brings real CHARACTER to a living room — without a penny spent on a decorator…

So — key takeaways: hourly rates run £30–£150, a single room costs around £1,000–£2,500, and a full home starts at £20,000… knowing these figures upfront means NO surprises…

Did you know styling your home doesn't have to be guesswork?

We've built a free set of Home Decor tools and styling guides…

From colour theory and design principles to gallery wall layouts and art sizing. Download them all from our site!

Find all you need to transform your home into a calming oasis!

Happy Decorating!
